about: Own-words reads from the daily research task (ADMIS, Rabobank, Czapp and the news feed). fund_score: -1 bearish to +1 bullish, a judgement on the fundamental news only.

corn.fundamental: Export demand stays the new positive after the marketing-year-high sales print, and Friday's broad grain rally lifted Dec to about 446. Slow Iowa harvest keeps some farmer selling off the market near term; the yield debate is unchanged.
events: Grains rally broadly Friday (AgWeb)
Corn export sales post a marketing-year high (MarketWatch)
Heavy rain leaves Iowa harvest behind schedule (AgroLatam)

soybeans.fundamental: Fresh export announcements pushed beans to a two-week high and Jan holds about 1,233, above the long-term momentum trigger. China buying is now the main driver; CONAB left Brazil's crop estimates unchanged, so no offset from South America this week.
events: Soybeans hit two-week high on export announcements (Investing.com, Barchart)
CONAB holds off on Brazil soybean and corn changes (Brownfield)
Farm groups press for removal of remaining China tariffs (RFD-TV)

meal.fundamental: Meal is riding the soybean rally and is up about 1.5%, testing 330.7 resistance; no meal-specific supply news.
events: Soybean complex rallies on export sales (Barchart)
Dec meal ~330, at first resistance (desk quote)

oil.fundamental: Demand signals are mixed: Chevron restarting its Ralston biodiesel plant adds feedstock demand, while state requests for renewable-fuel waivers threaten blending volumes. Brazil's Petrobras is expanding in biofuels logistics.
events: Chevron to restart Ralston, Iowa biodiesel plant (Successful Farming)
Biofuel groups warn state RFS waiver requests threaten grain demand (Successful Farming)
Petrobras buying out Logum partners to expand biofuels logistics (Reuters)

wheat.fundamental: Nothing new on supply or demand: China is still sourcing French and Argentine wheat. Friday's bounce has carried Dec through the 593 resistance at about 594, which reads as short covering alongside corn and beans after new lows, not fresh export business.
events: Dec Chicago wheat trades through 593 resistance midday (desk quote)
Grains rally broadly Friday after Thursday's lows (AgWeb, Barchart)
China books French and Argentine wheat (Bloomberg)

kc.fundamental: Same as Chicago: the rebound to about 632 takes KC over its first resistance, but cheap competing origins still cap US export demand, so this looks like position squaring.
events: KC Dec trades above 629.50 resistance (desk quote)
Wheat follows the broad grain rally Friday (AgWeb)
China sources wheat from France and Argentina (Bloomberg)

cotton.fundamental: New since the model: trade-deal headlines point to firmer US export demand, while Texas growers report low yields and high fuel costs that reinforce the abandonment story. Old-crop Dec is near 79 with Mar about 3.9¢ over; that wide carry into Dec delivery says the market expects certificated cotton to show up, which is not a comfortable backdrop for Dec longs.
events: Trade deals seen opening room for more US cotton and rice exports (Brownfield)
Texas growers squeezed by high fuel costs and poor yields (RFD-TV, Farm Progress)
USDA trimmed its cotton crop estimate earlier this week (Brownfield)

hogs.fundamental: Hogs rallied Friday with Dec near 55.5, but the pork cutout near a five-year low keeps demand the weak link; the bounce looks like short covering.
events: Hogs rallying on Friday (Barchart)
Pork cutout stays near five-year low (The Pig Site)

cattle.fundamental: Fundamentals unchanged (rising beef imports vs. solid demand), but the market has turned: Dec is back near 220.75, above resistance and the 60-day momentum trigger, and the week looks set to close higher after a midday correction, suggesting the recent low is in.
events: Cattle correct midday but a higher week confirms the lows (AgWeb)
Beef imports pressuring beef prices (ADMIS)
US beef exports climb in September (Farm Progress)

feeders.fundamental: Feeders keep leading: Jan is around 335, above its 200-day average, helped by firmer corn being shrugged off. Cheaper beef-on-dairy calves remain the main cap on upside.
events: Jan feeders clear the 200-day average Friday (desk quote)
Higher week for cattle confirms the lows (AgWeb)
Beef-on-dairy calf prices dropping (Dairy Herd)

class3.fundamental: Dry whey jumped to $0.91 at the CME spot session, a support for Class III after Thursday's cheese drop. Bird flu keeps turning up in new dairy states, a herd-health risk that could slow milk growth if it spreads further.
events: CME spot dry whey jumps to $0.91; dairy mixed (Brownfield)
HPAI spreads to new states as dairy cases climb (Dairy Herd)
States push USDA to allow dairy bird-flu vaccines (Farm Progress)

class4.fundamental: Spot dairy was mixed Friday after Thursday's butter-led drop; strong protein demand is encouraging milk expansion, which weighs on butter and powder. HPAI spread is the main upside supply risk.
events: CME dairy prices mixed Friday (Brownfield)
Protein demand driving milk production growth (Brownfield)
HPAI spreads to new states (Dairy Herd)

palm.fundamental: 1 headline in the last 30 hours; the news flow leans supportive (supply risks or firm demand outnumber bearish supply news), prices mostly reported higher (1 supply-tight, 0 supply-loose, 1 up, 0 down by keyword).
events: Palm Oil Climbs as El Niño Threatens Indonesia’s 2027 Supplies (Bloomberg.com, 2026-11-12)

natgas.fundamental: Henry Hub is giving back part of the week's gain: Dec slipped to about 3.21, below 3.23 support, as the Hormuz LNG-tanker incident lifts global LNG risk but does little for prompt US balances. Longer-term LNG export capacity remains the support.
events: Dec gas dips below 3.23 support midday (desk quote)
Iran says LNG tanker hit mine in Hormuz (Reuters)
Natural gas still on track for a sizable weekly gain (ADMIS)

crude.fundamental: Brent is back above $96 as Iran tensions rise again, while the US side keeps adding supply (record output, rig count steady at 463). WTI holds near 88.8; the risk premium is doing the work against a looser physical balance.
events: Brent climbs back above $96 on Iran escalation (OilPrice.com)
US oil rig count holds at 463 as output hits another record (OilPrice.com)
Iraq October output highest since 2019 (Bloomberg/IEA)

ulsd.fundamental: Farm diesel prices are easing for the first time this fall, but refiners in Asia are returning to Gulf crude despite war risks and jet fuel costs remain extreme, keeping middle distillates tight.
events: Farmers see first break in diesel prices this fall (Brownfield)
Asian refiners turn back to Gulf oil (OilPrice.com)
Asian airlines face high jet fuel costs (OilPrice.com)

rbob.fundamental: No new headlines for this market in the last 30 hours.
events: Crude rebounded after Trump said a deal with Iran is not needed (OilPrice.com).
California refinery closures are reshaping West Coast flows (OilPrice.com).
